newsitem.title: GERMANY: Degussa H1 profit up 25 pct, sees good H2.
newsitem.headline: Degussa H1 profit up 25 pct, sees good H2.

text.p: Germany's Degussa AG on Tuesday predicted its earnings would remain favourable in the second half of its 1996/1997 business year after pretax profit grew 25 percent in the first six months.
"The growth momentum is coming mainly from abroad," Degussa said in a statement. It said earnings increased in all its business segments.
The chemicals and precious metals group said pretax proft in the six months to March 31 rose to 233 million marks ($134.6 million) from 186 million in the year-ago period.
Group sales rose five percent to 7.2 billion marks from 6.86 billion, Degussa said in a statement. The company's full year runs to September 30.
"After the pleasing first half we expect the earnings situation to remain good overall in the course of the year," Degussa said.

Sales of chemical products rose eight percent to 2.0 billion marks due entirely to increases in volume sales, with a one percent fall in prices compensated for by the positive impact of exchange rates, Degussa said.
Sales of health and nutrition products rose by 12 percent to 1.5 billion marks while earnings grew "significantly," Degussa said.

While health unit Asta Medica AG was hit by unsatisfactory domestic business the profit contribution of foreign drugs affiliates rose sharply, boosted by the first time consolidation of U.S. company Muro Pharmaceutical which Degussa bought last year, Degussa said.
The news failed to spur the company's shares which first rose then fell 0.50 marks or 0.6 percent to 79.50 marks in electronic trade after the earnings announcement.
Dealers said the shares had succumbed to profit-taking after having risen in anticipation of good first-half results.
They also noted that while the earnings were at the upper end of forecasts, sales were at the lower end, suggesting a possible slowdown in business in the second half.

But Banque Paribas reiterated its "Buy" recommendation for the stock, noting that the 29 percent rise in parent company pretax profit to 86 million marks in the first half was a sign that Degussa's domestic situation was improving.
Degussa's precious metals and banking division had a two percent rise in sales to 3.7 billion marks in the first half. Precious metals trading revenues rose by eight percent to 1.9 billion marks.
